script_line: It costs about eight dollars. / Eight dollars is not really a price.
evidence: Steam store page (app 4001890) lists base game at $7.99; released Aug 20, 2026. Launch week had a 38% intro discount (~$4.95 until Aug 27), now ended. Bundles exist but base game is $7.99. Price may change with sales; 'about eight dollars' is safe.

claim: Makers hoped it might sell 200,000 copies
script_line: Its makers hoped it might sell two hundred thousand copies.
evidence: Sweden Game Arena quotes Melvin Olsson: 'Our goal was to sell around 200,000 copies.' Sweden Game Arena is a secondary source relaying the founders; the original is a developer interview.

claim: By early October one analytics firm estimated more than ten million
script_line: By early October, one analytics firm estimated more than ten million.
evidence: Alinea Analytics Substack post dated Oct 01, 2026 says 'now 10.1M copies sold overall' (also $19.3M in September, over $50M total). It is a third-party estimate; the developer itself only announced 1M (players/copies, wording varies) on Aug 22. Script attributes correctly. Searches on Oct 11 found no newer figure, but Alinea's October update (early Nov) will likely supersede it, and the video may publish after that. Note: the phrase has no noun; 'ten million' implicitly copies, which matches Alinea.
minimal_fix_if_needed: Optional: 'more than ten million copies' to make the unit explicit (Alinea says copies, not players). If publishing after early Nov, recheck Alinea's October update.

claim: Everyone in the boat buys their own copy (no Friend Pass)
script_line: Everyone in the boat buys their own copy.
evidence: The Steam page text retrieved mentions no Friend Pass or free guest mode, and the game is sold as 1-4 player co-op, so own-copy is consistent. But this is absence of evidence from a page summary, not an affirmative statement from the developer; no article I opened states it either. A Friend Pass or Steam Remote Play Together could still exist and Steam-side Remote Play lets one owner host friends, which is a known loophole for many co-op games.
minimal_fix_if_needed: Soften: 'Everyone in the boat usually buys their own copy.' Or, before recording, open the Steam page by eye and confirm there is no Friend Pass and check the Remote Play Together tag.

script_line: The developers' own description on Steam reads, word for word: "cartoon violence towards fish and gambling with fish... (no real money)."
evidence: Exact Steam wording: 'This game includes cartoon violence towards fish and gambling with fish (no real money)'. There is NO ellipsis between 'fish' and '(no real money)'. The script's '...' is not in the original, so 'word for word' is false at that point. (Also it is the developer-written mature content descriptor, which is correctly called their own description.)
minimal_fix_if_needed: Remove the ellipsis: "cartoon violence towards fish and gambling with fish (no real money)." (Keep the pause in the voice delivery, not in the quote.)

script_line: They are slapping each other in the face. / ...the way you bring them back is by picking them up... and slapping them in the face.
evidence: GamingOnLinux: a teammate can 'pick you up and slap you in the face a few times to bring you back to life.' InGameNews and Dot Esports say the same.
Coverage says players 'annihilate fish with snipers' and boss guides recommend a sniper rifle (Albatross, Tuna). The hook correctly avoids the earlier unverified 'seagulls' detail.

script_line: Gambling the fish money. / You sell your catch. You gamble the money. / Someone gambles the savings
evidence: Steam says gambling is a feature (descriptor 'gambling with fish'); coverage describes a roulette table where players sell fish or gamble them. GamingOnLinux describes a slot machine paying weapon skins, so mechanic details differ by article; the script does not name a game type. Technically players gamble fish/catch rather than cash, but 'fish money' and 'gamble the money' is loose, not false.

claim: Begin with simple tools, soon heavy weapons
script_line: You begin with simple tools. Soon you have heavy weapons.
evidence: Steam: 'You start with no gear or weapons and earn money to buy better equipment.' Coverage lists knives, knuckle dusters, guns, dynamite/explosives, shotguns and sniper rifles. 'Heavy weapons' is a stretch if it implies rocket launchers or miniguns (not found in sources); 'simple tools' vs 'no gear' is a minor mismatch.
minimal_fix_if_needed: 'You begin with almost nothing. Soon you have guns and dynamite.' (or keep 'heavy weapons' only if a shotgun/sniper/dynamite count for the Producer; keep image generic, no rocket launchers on screen).

evidence: Steam: you can fight bosses; sources name Piranha, Pufferfish, Albatross, Tuna, Whale.

claim: Someone gets launched across the island / falls in the water
script_line: Someone gets launched across the island by something they absolutely should not have poked.
evidence: Steam says it is a physics-based fishing simulator and coverage mentions 'chaotic physics' and a viral clip of a player's body carried off by a seagull, but I found no source stating players are launched across an island. The 'ragdoll launch' dossier anchor is not confirmed by the sources reached. Falling in the water is plausible (crash onto island, boats) but not explicitly sourced either.
minimal_fix_if_needed: Use a sourced line: 'Someone gets slapped. Someone gets carried off by a seagull.' (seagull abduction viral clip per Mein-MMO) or 'Someone gets sent flying by the physics' if the Producer confirms a clip. Otherwise mark as generic comedic exaggeration and show no gameplay footage.

script_line: Friendslop. Half a joke, half an insult. Cheap, chaotic co-op games built for playing with friends.
evidence: Term coined as a joking X post in March 2025 (Lethal Company, Content Warning, R.E.P.O.); 'friend' + 'slop', often used with a sneer, some developers embraced it. Definition matches Wikipedia/KnowYourMeme/Creative Bloq. How to Fish is labelled friendslop in reviews.

claim: Two friends who founded the studio met in high school
script_line: the two friends who founded the studio behind it? They met in high school.
evidence: Sweden Game Arena: Carl-Vilhelm Johansson and Melvin Olsson met at LBS Kreativa Gymnasiet, Gothenburg, and founded Dazed Games in 2024. No source confirms a headcount; founders did most work with outside help (Patrik Carlsson sound, Martin Weidenborn music); funded in part by Landfall per LinkedIn posts. Script never says the team is only two people; some outlets (DLCompare, Xiaomi) call it a two-person studio, but do not echo that. Keep the claim about the founders only.

claim: First paid game had not done well
script_line: Their first paid game had not done well.
evidence: Sweden Game Arena: first game Out of Hand: Deluxe, free on Steam first; paid version summer 2025 sold below expectations. 'First paid game' is accurate (free version came first).

script_line: By early October ... more than ten million; $8; millions of people
evidence: (a) Alinea's next update (early Nov) will supersede 10.1M; 'by early October' is time-stamped so it stays true. (b) Developer-confirmed number is only 1M (Aug 22), reported as copies or players by different outlets; 10.1M is third-party. (c) Another tracker (Raijin) showed a far lower early estimate; GameDiscoverCo put August at 6.3M units, so estimates vary but 10M+ by Oct is consistent in order of magnitude. (d) Price could drop in seasonal sales. (e) Steam peak concurrents vary 268K-374K by source: do not use. (f) Player cap said 1-4 on Steam; script correctly avoids a number ('a few friends').
minimal_fix_if_needed: Keep 'one analytics firm estimated' attribution and the 'by early October' stamp; put the Alinea source on screen. Recheck right before publish.
